season.evidence: Ascents by month peak Jul-Sep (99 of ~120). Web search of WTA and Mountaineers reports: late-June traverses found snow at the gap, mid-July through early September is good, late September and October get cold.

otherTracksConsidered.why: Round trip from trailhead but also climbs Hinman the same day.
Trailhead round trip that also includes Hinman (highest point there).
Camp-based, finishes at the trailhead after Hinman; not a clean single-peak round trip.
Walk up from La Bohn Gap camp; no trailhead start.
Camp-based at La Bohn Lakes, no trailhead start.

facts.text: In late September, strong wind can hit the final summit ridge hard enough to push you around; carry a windproof layer.
In September several cairned paths cross the upper talus and are easier to spot on the way down than going up; none is required.

notes: Only La Bohn East Ridge on this peak; no qualifying track because every summited trailhead start combined it with Hinman and every other track began from camp.
